key_insight: An exciton-kinetics coupled drift-diffusion model shows that CT-CS energy alignment, more than LE-CT or LE-T offsets, is the main control knob for balancing charge generation and voltage loss in organic photovoltaics.
engineering_relevance: The model gives device engineers a practical way to tune donor–acceptor energetics and triplet recycling kinetics to improve photocurrent while limiting open-circuit voltage penalties.
method: Self-consistent exciton kinetics + drift-diffusion coupling for singlet/triplet states
Solves reversible photophysical transitions and state populations under transient and steady-state conditions
Analyzes LE-CT, CT-CS, and LE-T offsets plus triplet-transfer pathways
evidence_signal: The framework reproduces reported triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends, supporting the model against experimental device behavior.
watch_item: Triplet-recycling benefits depend strongly on CT-T kinetics and temperature, so small energetic misalignment can quickly degrade performance or make separation highly sensitive to operating conditions.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
